course_description:
This course will consider the financial management of financial institutions and the assessment of credit risk as applied to bank lending. Considerable industry involvement through guest lecturers and presenters will result in a practical understanding of risks assessment, financial distress prediction, asset/liability management, securitisation, bank regulation, bank profitability and the international banking system.

The course will also help students develop a broad understanding of how financial institutions operate and covers the traditional role of financial institutions, including banks and funds, and how their operation has changed in recent years. Understanding regulation, risk management and performance measurement are some of the key tasks. Securitisation, corporate capital raising, the role of credit rating agencies, and sales and trading of derivatives are explored. The course is delivered in seminar blocks with scheduled guest industry expert lecturers.

assessment_details.title: Individual Research Assignment
assessment_details.task_description: In the individual research assignment, students are to research specific topic areas. Students will be rewarded for information gathered outside of the seminar content and developing arguments based on the evidence they have collected. Students will need to read academic papers as well as regulatory information to answer short answer, essay style and numerical questions. It will involve the use of Excel, and a bibliography will be required. Further details on the assignment will be provided on the Blackboard site. The assignment will have a maximum word count of 3,000 words (subject to change). Read full task description Hide full task description
